records.claim_text: SAP splits its table controls into two families: fully responsive tables (responsive table, list, tree) and desktop-centric tables (analytical, grid, tree table).
records.evidence_quote: Fully responsive tables are the responsive table, list, and tree.
records.own_words_restatement: Pick from one of two control families depending on whether the screen must reflow on small viewports or is desktop-only.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Determines whether the WBS list and the WBS workbench use different table controls.

records.claim_text: The desktop-centric table family is explicitly named as the analytical table, grid table and tree table, optimised for large data sets but not fully responsive.
records.evidence_quote: Desktop-centric tables are the analytical table, grid table, and tree table.
records.own_words_restatement: Three heavier grid-style controls exist for volume work and are not expected to reflow to phone widths.
records.applicability_to_our_build: A WBS workbench targeting desktop planners can legitimately use a non-responsive grid family.

records.claim_text: The responsive table is guided to about 200 items of average complexity; the limit is on data loaded at any point, not rows in the database.
records.evidence_quote: the responsive table can handle up to 200 items
records.own_words_restatement: Treat roughly two hundred loaded rows as the practical ceiling for the reflowing table control.
records.applicability_to_our_build: A WBS with more than ~200 loaded nodes should not use the reflowing table control.

records.claim_text: SAP states the single selection criterion for the tree table is that data needs to be displayed in a hierarchical manner.
records.evidence_quote: Data needs to be displayed in a hierarchical manner.
records.own_words_restatement: Hierarchy is the only stated reason to choose the tree grid over the flat grid.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Directly justifies a tree grid for the WBS hierarchy.

records.claim_text: The analytical table is selected when multilevel grouping plus grand totals and subtotals are required.
records.evidence_quote: You need multilevel grouping as well as grand totals and subtotals.
records.own_words_restatement: Choose the aggregating grid only when the screen must roll up numbers across group levels.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS cost roll-up screens are the analytical-grid case; the WBS structure itself is the tree case.

records.claim_text: Desktop-centric tables allow only one control per cell, only single-row templates, and require all rows to have the same height.
records.evidence_quote: Only one control can be added per cell.
records.own_words_restatement: The grid family trades layout freedom for scroll performance: one widget per cell, uniform row height.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Rich multi-datapoint WBS cells cannot be delivered in the grid family.

records.claim_text: In desktop-centric tables vertical scrolling is not smooth because row content is exchanged rather than truly scrolled, for performance reasons.
records.evidence_quote: Vertical scrolling is not smooth.
records.own_words_restatement: The grid family recycles a fixed set of row DOM nodes as the viewport moves.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Any WBS grid we build should virtualise rows the same way rather than render all nodes.

records.claim_text: The tree table is optimised for fast scrolling only within the first 1000 items, which is the documented performance boundary for hierarchy screens.
records.evidence_quote: The tree table is optimized to allow faster scrolling within the first 1000 items.
records.own_words_restatement: Beyond roughly a thousand visible nodes, scroll responsiveness in a hierarchy grid degrades.
records.applicability_to_our_build: HARD CONSTRAINT: the WBS workbench must keep the expanded node count near or under 1000, via collapsed defaults and lazy child loading.

records.topic: When a tree table is appropriate
records.claim_text: SAP advises showing large hierarchical trees only as a last resort, preferring chunked navigation or drilldown charts instead.
records.evidence_quote: you should only show trees with a lot of hierarchical data as a last resort
records.own_words_restatement: Dense hierarchies read as complex; break them into navigable chunks where the task allows.
records.applicability_to_our_build: The WBS workbench should offer level-scoped drilldown views alongside the full tree, not only the full tree.

records.claim_text: A tree table is available for desktops and tablets but not smartphone sizes, requiring a separate adaptive UI for phones.
records.evidence_quote: A tree table is available for desktops and tablets, but not in smartphone sizes.
records.own_words_restatement: Hierarchy grids are a desktop and tablet control; phones need a different screen.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Mobile WBS access needs a separate reduced-scope screen, not a squeezed tree.

records.claim_text: In a tree table the hierarchical column is always first and cannot be dragged to another position.
records.evidence_quote: The tree column is always the first column and cannot be dragged.
records.own_words_restatement: Column reordering must exclude the indenting column that carries the hierarchy.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our WBS column personalisation must pin the WBS-element column.

records.claim_text: Freeze is offered in the column header menu and freezing one column freezes every column from the first up to the selected one.
records.evidence_quote: The Freeze/Unfreeze option is provided in the column header menu of all columns.
records.own_words_restatement: Freezing is a left-edge boundary, not a per-column toggle.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Implement freeze as a boundary index, exposed from the column header menu.

records.claim_text: In tree and grid tables all line items must have the same height to avoid adverse side effects when scrolling vertically.
records.evidence_quote: all line items must have the same height
records.own_words_restatement: Virtualised scrolling assumes a constant row height; wrapping text breaks it.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS descriptions must truncate, not wrap, inside the grid.

records.claim_text: The tree table does not compute filter results itself; it sends a filter request and displays whatever the service returns.
records.evidence_quote: The tree table itself has no influence on the filter result.
records.own_words_restatement: Filtering a hierarchy is a backend concern; the client only renders the returned subtree.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our WBS filter must be resolved server-side, returning pruned nodes plus their surviving ancestors.

records.claim_text: SAP's recommended hierarchy filter approach is to remove leaves that fail the criteria and then remove nodes left empty.
records.evidence_quote: Remove all leaves that don’t fit the filter criteria
records.own_words_restatement: Filter the leaves first, then discard branches that no longer contain anything.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Defines the WBS filter algorithm precisely.

records.claim_text: Where the hierarchy structure must stay stable, SAP advises sorting only leaves and not nodes.
records.evidence_quote: sort only leaves, but not nodes
records.own_words_restatement: Preserve branch order when the structure itself carries meaning; reorder only within a branch.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS numbering order is meaningful, so sorting must be scoped inside a parent.

records.claim_text: SAP advises deliberately choosing the initial expand or collapse state, collapsing the whole tree when many root-level items exist.
records.evidence_quote: it might make sense to collapse the whole tree in the beginning
records.own_words_restatement: Set the opening depth to the level the user actually works at, not always fully open.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Combined with the 1000-item boundary, our WBS should open collapsed to level 2 by default.

records.claim_text: SAP strongly recommends the multi-selection plug-in over multi-toggle so that Select All and range selections include items not yet loaded in the front end.
records.evidence_quote: We strongly recommend using the multi-selection plug-in.
records.own_words_restatement: Bulk selection must reason about the whole result set, not only rendered rows.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our mass-action model must express selection as a query, not a list of loaded row ids.

records.claim_text: Range selection in the grid and tree tables is capped by a configurable limit whose documented default is 200 items.
records.evidence_quote: limited to the specified number of items (default = 200)
records.own_words_restatement: Cap how many rows one shift-range can select, and notify the user when the cap bites.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Set an explicit mass-action cap for WBS elements and surface it in the UI.

records.claim_text: In multi-toggle mode the Select All checkbox only selects items currently loaded in the front end, so later-loaded rows appear unselected.
records.evidence_quote: selects or deselects all items that are currently loaded in the front end
records.own_words_restatement: Naive Select All is scoped to what is loaded, which surprises users on paged data.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our Select All must state its scope explicitly (page vs all matching).

records.claim_text: The grid table supports an unlimited number of rows with lazy loading but is optimised for fast scrolling only within the first 1000 items.
records.evidence_quote: The grid table is optimized to allow faster scrolling within the first 1000 items.
records.own_words_restatement: Unbounded row counts are supported, but the fast-scroll window is about a thousand rows.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Same boundary as the tree grid; page or filter beyond it.

records.claim_text: SAP names working on more than 1,000 rows as a reason to choose the analytical table over the responsive table.
records.evidence_quote: You have to work on more than 1,000 rows.
records.own_words_restatement: Above about a thousand rows, the aggregating grid architecture is the intended choice.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Large WBS cost reports belong in an aggregating grid.

records.claim_text: The analytical table requires analytical binding; without it the grid table is the fallback but loses grouping, aggregation and responsiveness.
records.evidence_quote: the grid table doesn’t provide grouping, aggregation options, and is not responsive
records.own_words_restatement: Server-side grouping and totals are a service capability, not a UI toggle.
records.applicability_to_our_build: If the Zoho ERP API cannot return grouped totals, our UI must compute or drop them explicitly.

records.claim_text: Grouping levels in the analytical table are less flexible than a tree when nodes at several levels contain children, so hierarchies belong in a tree table.
records.evidence_quote: Several grouping levels are possible.
records.own_words_restatement: Multi-level grouping flattens attribute values; it does not model a real parent-child structure.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Do not model WBS parentage as grouping columns.

records.claim_text: SAP routes table personalisation by column count: view settings and table personalisation dialogs below about 20 columns, the P13n dialog above that.
records.evidence_quote: The user is able to personalize more than about 20 columns.
records.own_words_restatement: Roughly twenty columns is the threshold between simple and full personalisation UIs.
records.applicability_to_our_build: A wide WBS grid crosses this threshold and needs the full personalisation dialog.

records.claim_text: Sorting, filtering and grouping live in the view settings dialog while show/hide and reorder of columns live in the table personalisation dialog.
records.evidence_quote: The table personalization dialog can show/hide and reorder columns.
records.own_words_restatement: Column layout and data ordering are separate personalisation surfaces in the simple pattern.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our settings dialog can merge both into tabs, matching the full personalisation pattern.

records.claim_text: All table personalisation dialogs are opened from a Settings button positioned on the right-hand side of the table toolbar.
records.evidence_quote: All table personalization dialogs are opened via the Settings button on the right-hand side
records.own_words_restatement: One consistent gear affordance at the trailing edge of the table toolbar.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Place our WBS grid settings affordance in the same slot.

records.claim_text: SAP advises using a filter bar rather than an in-dialog filter tab when a very complex filter is needed.
records.evidence_quote: A very complex filter is needed. In this case, consider using a filter bar instead
records.own_words_restatement: Persistent, always-visible filtering beats a buried dialog tab once criteria get rich.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS search screens should expose a persistent filter bar.

records.claim_text: SAP now labels variants as views in the user interface while retaining variant terminology at control level.
records.evidence_quote: we now call variants “views”, which is better understood by end users
records.own_words_restatement: Call the saved-settings object a view in the UI even if the code calls it a variant.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Use Views in our WBS UI labels.

records.claim_text: Exactly one default view can exist per variant management control and the user changes it in the Manage Views dialog.
records.evidence_quote: There can only be one default view
records.own_words_restatement: One view per user is flagged as the one applied on app start.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our view store needs a per-user single default flag.

records.claim_text: Public views are visible to everyone with app access; a public view can be edited by its creator and by key users only.
records.evidence_quote: Public views are visible to all users who have access to the app.
records.own_words_restatement: Sharing is a boolean on the view plus an ownership rule for editing.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our WBS view model needs owner_id, is_public and an admin override role.

records.claim_text: The pre-shipped standard view is the minimum vendor-delivered filter set and cannot be modified or deleted by users.
records.evidence_quote: The standard view is the minimum set of filters delivered by SAP
records.own_words_restatement: Ship an unmodifiable baseline view users can always fall back to.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Ship a read-only Standard WBS view as the reset target.

records.claim_text: Views carry an Apply Automatically flag that runs the view immediately on selection, discouraged when the selection causes long loading times.
records.evidence_quote: If checked, the view is applied immediately whenever it is selected.
records.own_words_restatement: Let the user decide whether picking a view also triggers the query.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Needed for expensive WBS roll-up views.

records.claim_text: When the user changes settings covered by the active view, the view name is marked with an asterisk to indicate unsaved changes.
records.evidence_quote: the view is marked with an asterisk (*) to indicate the unsaved changes
records.own_words_restatement: A single glyph on the view title communicates unsaved personalisation.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Cheap, high-value affordance for the WBS workbench header.

records.claim_text: SAP recommends a single page-level variant management control saving filters, tabs, tables and charts, with control-level variants only as an exception.
records.evidence_quote: we recommend using one variant management control for the whole page
records.own_words_restatement: One saved view should capture the whole screen state, not each widget separately.
records.applicability_to_our_build: The WBS workbench view should serialise filter + columns + expansion depth together.

records.claim_text: Mandatory filters are marked with an asterisk next to the label and must carry values for the search to return results.
records.evidence_quote: An asterisk next to the filter label indicates the filter is mandatory.
records.own_words_restatement: Required criteria are marked inline and preset so the first load does not error.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Project code should be a preset mandatory WBS filter.

records.claim_text: The Adapt Filters entry point shows the number of active filters in parentheses, and a filter can be active without being visible in the bar.
records.evidence_quote: the number of active filters is displayed in parentheses
records.own_words_restatement: Show how many criteria are actually constraining the result, including hidden ones.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Prevents the silent-hidden-filter bug class in the WBS list.

records.claim_text: SAP prefers live update mode, where results refresh on each input change, over manual mode requiring a Go button.
records.evidence_quote: Whenever possible, use the live update mode because it is more convenient
records.own_words_restatement: Auto-refresh on change unless the query is expensive; then require explicit submission.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Expensive WBS roll-ups justify a Go button; simple lists should live-update.

records.claim_text: SAP directs teams to use the filter bar's basic search field for keyword search and not to show a search field in the table toolbar.
records.evidence_quote: Use the basic search field to provide a keyword search.
records.own_words_restatement: One search box per screen, attached to the filter area, not duplicated on the table.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Avoid two competing WBS search fields.

records.claim_text: The value help dialog is chosen over the select dialog when the user must define conditions such as ranges and exclusions.
records.evidence_quote: The user needs to define conditions, such as ranges and exclusions.
records.own_words_restatement: Condition-building (operators, ranges, exclusions) is what separates the richer picker from the simple one.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS code range pickers need the condition-capable variant.

records.claim_text: Selected items and conditions in the value help dialog are shown as tokens, with inclusion and exclusion distinguished by operators rather than colour.
records.evidence_quote: The selected items and conditions are displayed in a tokenizer
records.own_words_restatement: Represent each chosen value or condition as a removable chip labelled with its operator.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Non-colour differentiation of include/exclude is also an accessibility win.

records.claim_text: The select dialog offers a list of entries plus a search field for picking one or more items from a comprehensive list.
records.evidence_quote: The select dialog comes with a list of entries and a search field
records.own_words_restatement: Searchable list picker, no operators; full-screen on phones, popover elsewhere.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Suffices for picking a single WBS parent.

records.claim_text: SAP Fiori defines five semantic colours tied to predefined value states, and a separate generic industry palette with no fixed meaning.
records.evidence_quote: SAP Fiori has five semantic colors
records.own_words_restatement: A small closed set of meaning-bearing colours plus an open industry palette you must define yourself.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Define exactly five WBS status colours and document their meaning; no ad hoc colours.

records.claim_text: Colour alone is never sufficient: SAP requires an accompanying text such as an object status for every colour used to convey meaning.
records.evidence_quote: All colors require a corresponding descriptive text for accessibility purposes.
records.own_words_restatement: Every coloured status must also carry a readable label, so meaning survives without colour perception.
records.applicability_to_our_build: HARD RULE for WBS status chips: colour + label, always.

records.claim_text: The generic industry (indication) colour palette is supported exclusively by tables and the object status, and the two palettes cannot be mixed.
records.evidence_quote: The indication color palette is supported exclusively by tables and the object status.
records.own_words_restatement: Extended status colours are only available on a couple of controls, and only one palette at a time.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Constrains any attempt at a many-colour WBS status scheme.

records.claim_text: Object status is a short semantically coloured text representing an object's status, with an optional icon and no generic neutral icon available.
records.evidence_quote: Object status: a short text that represents the semantic status of an object
records.own_words_restatement: A compact coloured text badge is the standard status element inside rows and headers.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Use one status component for WBS element status everywhere.

records.claim_text: A UI element can carry only one value state at any given time, and value states are rendered using the theme's semantic colours by default.
records.evidence_quote: A UI element can have only one value state at any given time.
records.own_words_restatement: Resolve competing statuses to one winning state before rendering.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Need a documented precedence order for WBS row states (error over warning over info).

records.claim_text: Mass editing lets users change multiple objects that share editable properties, using a dialog of combo boxes and select controls.
records.evidence_quote: Mass editing is done in a dialog containing combo boxes and select controls.
records.own_words_restatement: Select rows, press Edit, get one dialog with a dropdown per editable column.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Blueprint for bulk WBS attribute changes.

records.claim_text: Mass edit dropdowns carry sentinel entries such as Keep Existing Values and Leave Blank, with Leave Blank preselected for empty columns.
records.evidence_quote: the option < Leave Blank > is preselected
records.own_words_restatement: Bulk edit must distinguish leave-alone, clear, and set-to-value as three explicit choices.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Critical tri-state semantics for our bulk WBS update payloads.

records.claim_text: All micro charts are fully responsive, sizing to their parent container, and only XS bullet, comparison and stacked-bar micro charts are permitted inside grid and tree table cells.
records.evidence_quote: All micro charts are fully responsive.
records.own_words_restatement: Tiny non-interactive charts can live in cells, but only a short list of types in the grid family.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS progress in a grid cell should be a bullet-style micro chart, not a full chart.

records.claim_text: The bullet micro chart shows data points for given points in time and must not be used to show a time series.
records.evidence_quote: Do not use it to show a time series.
records.own_words_restatement: Actual-vs-target comparison is a bullet; change over time is a line, area or column.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Planned-vs-actual WBS cost is a bullet; burn-down over time is not.

records.claim_text: Export to Spreadsheet is limited by available browser memory and SAP directs teams to custom exporters for large tables.
records.evidence_quote: The file size of the exported file is limited by the available browser memory.
records.own_words_restatement: Browser-built spreadsheets crash on large data; big exports must be produced server-side.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Full-project WBS exports must be a backend job, not a client download.

records.claim_text: The export takes back-end values by default and does not apply front-end formatters, so key-value pairs must be configured to match on-screen text.
records.evidence_quote: SAPUI5 formatters (for example, for dates, times, and numbers) are not taken into account.
records.own_words_restatement: What you export is the raw value unless you explicitly map it to the displayed text.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our WBS export must map status codes to labels explicitly.

records.claim_text: Tree structures export using spreadsheet grouping for the first seven levels plus double indentation for all levels.
records.evidence_quote: tree structures are displayed using the grouping functionality (first seven levels) and double indentation
records.own_words_restatement: Hierarchy survives export as native spreadsheet outline groups up to seven levels, then as indentation only.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Directly specifies how a WBS export should encode depth.

records.claim_text: Empty states are handled by the illustrated message control and should tell the user what the state is for, why it appears, and what to do next.
records.evidence_quote: Empty states can be handled by the illustrated message control.
records.own_words_restatement: One component covers no-data, no-results and error-empty, each with tailored guidance text.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Three distinct WBS empty states: never created, filtered to nothing, failed to load.

records.claim_text: SAP advises avoiding empty tables, providing instructions for populating them, and removing the item count from the title when there are zero items.
records.evidence_quote: Remove the item count in the table title if there are zero items.
records.own_words_restatement: Suppress the count badge when nothing is shown, and explain how to add data.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Small polish detail for the WBS grid header.

records.claim_text: SAP forbids using a blocking busy dialog for app or page loading and instructs teams to set busy state at control or app level instead.
records.evidence_quote: Do not use the busy dialog for app or page loading.
records.own_words_restatement: Block only the region that is actually loading; keep the rest of the shell usable.
records.applicability_to_our_build: The WBS tree and detail pane must have independent busy states.

records.claim_text: Placeholder loading shows a generic skeleton page of grey animated boxes as a per-floorplan placeholder while content loads.
records.evidence_quote: skeleton pages are grey boxes with animations to indicate loading activity
records.own_words_restatement: Show the shape of the coming layout, not a spinner, during first load.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Use a skeleton for initial WBS workbench load, spinners only for in-place refresh.

records.claim_text: To signal that a table contains items with errors or warnings, SAP prescribes a message strip above the table, kept updated as issues change.
records.evidence_quote: show a message strip above the tree table
records.own_words_restatement: Aggregate row problems into one dismissible banner directly above the grid.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Validation errors after a WBS bulk save should surface here.

records.claim_text: SAP requires that every application and UI component be fully operable using the keyboard.
records.evidence_quote: Every application and UI component must be fully operable using the keyboard.
records.own_words_restatement: No interaction may be mouse-only, including drag-and-drop and column resize.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS reordering must have a keyboard path.

records.claim_text: In SAP Fiori all keyboard shortcut commands are captured by the application except Ctrl-L, which remains available to reach the browser address bar.
records.evidence_quote: all keyboard shortcut commands are captured by the application except Ctrl-L
records.own_words_restatement: The app owns the shortcut namespace apart from one reserved browser combination.
records.applicability_to_our_build: We can safely bind Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Enter etc. in the WBS workbench.

records.claim_text: Column width is adjusted with Shift plus arrow keys and column position with Ctrl plus arrow keys on the focused column header.
records.evidence_quote: The width of the focused column header can be increased with Shift+Right
records.own_words_restatement: Resize and reorder columns without a mouse, using modifier plus arrow on the header.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Concrete keybindings to implement in the WBS grid header.

records.claim_text: SAP states its default Fiori theme is designed against the international Web Content Accessibility Guidelines WCAG 2.2 minimum colour contrast requirements.
records.evidence_quote: Following the requirements of the international Web Content Accessibility Guidelines WCAG 2.2
records.own_words_restatement: WCAG 2.2 is the named external reference standard; SAP does not state a conformance level on this page.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Set our target as WCAG 2.2 AA. NOTE: the explicit level letter was NOT found on this page.

records.claim_text: SAP ships high-contrast themes that support a 7:1 contrast ratio for texts and are selectable in user settings, persisted as a preference.
records.evidence_quote: high-contrast themes that support the required contrast ratio of 7:1 for texts
records.own_words_restatement: A user-selectable high-contrast theme is part of the accessibility story, not an afterthought.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our token architecture must allow a high-contrast theme swap.

records.claim_text: The framework prepares screen reader support technically, but the actual structure and visible and invisible texts must be defined at application level.
records.evidence_quote: the actual visible and invisible texts, need to be defined at application level
records.own_words_restatement: A component library does not make an app accessible; labels and structure are ours to supply.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Budget explicit work for aria labelling of WBS rows and actions.

records.claim_text: SAP requires labels on a page to be unique, because screen readers list elements by label and duplicates make selection ambiguous.
records.evidence_quote: Make sure labels on a page are unique.
records.own_words_restatement: Repeated row actions named identically are unusable via assistive technology.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Per-row WBS action buttons need row-qualified accessible names.

records.claim_text: SAP's current theme is Morning Horizon, with Evening Horizon as an optional dark theme alongside the older Quartz Light and Quartz Dark themes.
records.evidence_quote: The latest theme for SAP applications is called Morning Horizon.
records.own_words_restatement: Horizon is the current visual generation; Quartz is the previous one, each with light and dark variants. NO SAP COLOUR VALUES ARE REPRODUCED HERE.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Concept only: our design system needs a light/dark pair per generation, not SAP's values.

records.claim_text: All UI components are specified via cross-technology design tokens mapped one-to-one to theming variables published as CSS variables, LESS, SASS and JSON.
records.evidence_quote: All of the user interface components are specified using cross-technology design tokens
records.own_words_restatement: Components reference semantic tokens; a theme is a set of values bound to those stable token names.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Adopt semantically named tokens so theme swaps require no component edits.

records.claim_text: SAP warns that individual colours should be changed only in exceptional cases, because changes must cover all element states and may break high-contrast modes.
records.evidence_quote: Change individual colors only in exceptional cases and after very careful consideration.
records.own_words_restatement: One-off colour overrides quietly break state variants and accessibility themes.
records.applicability_to_our_build: No hard-coded colours in WBS components; tokens only.

records.claim_text: SAP right-aligns numbers (excluding IDs and phone numbers), dates and times, and left-aligns text, IDs, URLs, email addresses and status information.
records.evidence_quote: Right-align numbers (except IDs and phone numbers), dates, and times.
records.own_words_restatement: Alignment is decided by data type, and identifier-like numbers are treated as text.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS code left, cost and dates right.

records.claim_text: SAP recommends the medium date format by default, with formats derived from the Unicode CLDR and locale-dependent ordering.
records.evidence_quote: based on the Unicode Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR)
records.own_words_restatement: Render dates from CLDR patterns for the user's locale; prefer the abbreviated-month form.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Never hard-code DD/MM/YYYY in the WBS UI.

records.claim_text: Date intervals must be delimited with an en dash rather than a minus sign.
records.evidence_quote: use an en dash “–” (not a minus sign) as a delimiter between the dates
records.own_words_restatement: Typographic detail that signals enterprise polish in schedule columns.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS start–finish columns.

records.claim_text: Number formatting covers integer, float, currency and percentage types, each with short, standard and long forms; standard is the general recommendation.
records.evidence_quote: Each data type can be formatted using a short, standard, or long format.
records.own_words_restatement: Abbreviated forms exist for tiles and dense cells; full precision is the default elsewhere.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS KPI tiles may abbreviate; the cost grid must not.

records.claim_text: The currency formatter accounts for currencies with three decimal places and rounds currency amounts down automatically.
records.evidence_quote: Currency amounts are rounded down automatically.
records.own_words_restatement: Decimal precision is a property of the currency, not a global setting, and display rounding truncates.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Display rounding must never feed back into stored WBS cost values.

records.claim_text: SAPUI5 derives right-to-left mode from the current language, defaulting to left-to-right, and exposes sap-ui-rtl as a configuration switch.
records.evidence_quote: SAPUI5 sets the RTL mode based on the current language
records.own_words_restatement: Direction follows locale automatically; an override switch exists for testing.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our WBS UI should set dir from locale, not from a separate user toggle.

records.claim_text: Changing directionality has a large impact on text-displaying controls, images and overall application alignment, and custom content must be tested separately.
records.evidence_quote: Changing the directionality has a big impact on text-displaying controls, images and the alignment
records.own_words_restatement: RTL is not a stylesheet flip; icons, indentation and custom CSS all need mirrored variants.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Tree indentation and expand chevrons in the WBS grid must mirror.

records.claim_text: Numeric content inside an RTL page must be forced to left-to-right using textDirection, with textAlign used for reversing text alignment.
records.evidence_quote: used for reversing the text alignment
records.own_words_restatement: WBS codes, phone numbers, currency amounts and dates keep LTR order inside an RTL layout.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS element codes must be rendered as LTR islands.

records.claim_text: Above 100 items the responsive table should use growing mode, loading additional items on scroll (preferred) or via a More button.
records.evidence_quote: To show more than 100 items, use the “growing” mode
records.own_words_restatement: One hundred rows is the point at which incremental loading becomes required.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Sets our default page size for flat WBS lists.

records.claim_text: SAP forbids showing aggregations in growing mode because it is unclear whether totals cover loaded items or all items.
records.evidence_quote: Don’t show aggregations in “growing” mode.
records.own_words_restatement: Client-side totals over a partially loaded set are misleading and must not be shown.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS cost totals must come from the server or the grid must not page.

records.claim_text: In auto pop-in mode columns have a default minimum width of 8 rem and low-priority columns move to the pop-in area first.
records.evidence_quote: The default minimum width per column is 8 rem.
records.own_words_restatement: Tag each column with an importance level so narrow viewports shed the least useful ones first.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Assign importance to every WBS column up front.

records.claim_text: The responsive table can pin its title bar, column headers and filter infobar to the top of the surrounding container while scrolling.
records.evidence_quote: the title bar, column headers, and filter infobar can stick to the top
records.own_words_restatement: Keep orientation chrome visible during long scrolls.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Mandatory for a deep WBS list.

records.claim_text: The table toolbar sits above the table and carries actions affecting the whole table plus actions applying to selected items, in a predefined group order.
records.evidence_quote: The table toolbar always appears above the table.
records.own_words_restatement: One toolbar above the grid holds table-scope and selection-scope actions in a stable order.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Defines the WBS grid action bar layout.

records.claim_text: An item counter can follow the table title in parentheses and is removed when no items are shown; selection can be surfaced alongside it.
records.evidence_quote: You can add an item counter after the title.
records.own_words_restatement: Show how many rows exist and how many are selected in the same title region.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Required feedback for WBS bulk actions.

records.claim_text: In tables a variant stores column layout, column visibility, sorting, filter settings and grouping, and variant management usually replaces the table title.
records.evidence_quote: a variant stores all the settings that define the table view
records.own_words_restatement: A saved view is exactly: visible columns, their order, sort, filter and grouping.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Precise schema for our saved-view record.

records.claim_text: SAP instructs teams not to move main actions into the toolbar overflow and to keep the predefined order for action groups.
records.evidence_quote: Don’t move main actions into the overflow.
records.own_words_restatement: Primary actions stay visible at every breakpoint; only secondary ones collapse.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Create WBS Element must never overflow.

records.claim_text: The infobar sits above the table showing applied filter criteria as labels or the number of selected items, and is hidden when no filter is applied.
records.evidence_quote: Do not show the infobar if no filter is applied.
records.own_words_restatement: A thin strip between toolbar and headers that names the constraints currently narrowing the data.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Prevents users misreading a filtered WBS as the whole WBS.

records.claim_text: The smart table generates a responsive, grid, tree or analytical table from an OData service and annotations, bundling personalisation, export and variant management.
records.evidence_quote: The smart table creates a responsive table, grid table, tree table, or analytical table
records.own_words_restatement: One metadata-driven wrapper renders any of the four table types with the standard feature bundle attached.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Argues for a single configurable WBS table component rather than four hand-built ones.

records.claim_text: SAP advises using variant management only if really needed, rather than adding it to every table by default.
records.evidence_quote: Use variant management only if really needed.
records.own_words_restatement: Saved views add cognitive and storage overhead; add them only where users really re-use configurations.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Views on the WBS workbench yes; on small embedded tables no.

records.claim_text: SAP explicitly excludes building a workbench or tools layout with the flexible column layout, directing teams to dynamic side content instead.
records.evidence_quote: You want to build a workbench or tools layout.
records.pattern_name: Workbench is not a column drilldown
records.own_words_restatement: A main working area with supporting side panels is a different layout from a progressive drilldown of columns.
records.applicability_to_our_build: HARD CONSTRAINT: the WBS workbench should be a main region plus collapsible side content, not a three-column drilldown.

records.claim_text: The compact density factor shrinks components to fit more information on screen and is intended for mouse and keyboard devices; most components default to cozy.
records.evidence_quote: Most components default to cozy.
records.own_words_restatement: Two (plus one condensed) sizing scales exist; you must actively choose one per device class.
records.applicability_to_our_build: The WBS workbench should ship compact on desktop by default.

records.claim_text: Condensed density must always be applied in addition to compact, never on its own and never mixed with cozy, or layout defects result.
records.evidence_quote: Do not use condensed on its own. Do not mix condensed with cozy.
records.own_words_restatement: The densest mode is an additive modifier on the compact scale, not a third independent scale.
records.applicability_to_our_build: If we offer an ultra-dense WBS view it must layer on compact.

records.claim_text: Neither compact nor condensed mode can be interacted with by touch, even on a desktop with a touchscreen.
records.evidence_quote: neither compact mode nor condensed mode can be interacted with touch
records.own_words_restatement: Dense rows produce targets too small for fingers; density must follow the real input device.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Detect touch capability before defaulting the WBS grid to compact.

records.claim_text: The status indicator should not be used inside a table; SAP directs teams to the progress indicator or radial micro chart there.
records.evidence_quote: Use the progress indicator or radial micro chart instead.
records.own_words_restatement: Row-level completion is shown by a progress bar or radial gauge, not by the icon-based indicator.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS percent-complete column should be a progress indicator.

records.claim_text: The table personalisation dialog is for a manageable number of columns and offers Reset, search, select-all and move-up/move-down reordering.
records.evidence_quote: the Reset button to revert to the initial state
records.own_words_restatement: Searchable checkbox list of columns, explicit move controls, and a reset to the shipped layout.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Reset-to-default is mandatory in our WBS column dialog.

records.claim_text: Selection behaviour is configurable as Row, RowSelector or RowOnly, chosen according to whether clicking a row is already used for navigation.
records.evidence_quote: An item is selected only by clicking the checkbox in the selector cell.
records.own_words_restatement: If a row click navigates, selection must be confined to the checkbox column.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS rows navigate to detail, so selection must be checkbox-only.

records.claim_text: SAP forbids disabling a row's selection checkbox; instead the user should be informed after the action is triggered if it cannot apply.
records.evidence_quote: Never disable the selection checkbox.
records.own_words_restatement: Selection stays uniformly available; eligibility is resolved and reported when the action runs.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Our bulk WBS actions need a per-item result report rather than pre-emptive row disabling.

records.claim_text: New items are placed relative to the selection: to the root if nothing is selected, into the selected node, or as a child of a selected leaf.
records.evidence_quote: If a single node is selected, add the new item to the selected node.
records.own_words_restatement: Where a new node lands is derived from what is selected, and a leaf becomes a node when given a child.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Exact insertion semantics for Add WBS Element.

records.claim_text: SAP escalates creation UI by column count: inline row, then dialog for up to eight editable columns, then a separate page beyond that.
records.evidence_quote: Open a dialog for larger tree tables with up to 8 editable columns.
records.own_words_restatement: Three creation affordances with a documented switch point at eight editable fields.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Decides whether WBS creation is inline, dialog or full page.

records.claim_text: Newly created rows pass through New, Recent and Added states, staying highlighted and pinned until the Added state restores normal sort and filter behaviour.
records.evidence_quote: Ignore current sort, filter, and grouping criteria to keep the item visible.
records.own_words_restatement: A just-created row is exempted from sorting and filtering so the user does not lose it.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Prevents the classic disappearing-new-WBS-node bug.

records.claim_text: SAP prescribes Ctrl+Enter (and ideally Enter) as the shortcut for triggering the Add or Create button on a table.
records.evidence_quote: Enable the shortcut Ctrl+Enter (and ideally Enter in addition)
records.own_words_restatement: Fast repeated row creation needs a keyboard trigger, not just a toolbar click.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Essential for rapid WBS entry.

records.claim_text: A context menu can be attached to a table, opened by right-click, long press, the context menu key or Shift+F10, and it overrides the browser menu.
records.evidence_quote: Context menus are opened by right-clicking (desktop), long press (mobile), the context menu key
records.own_words_restatement: Per-row commands can live in a context menu with a keyboard-reachable trigger.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Good home for WBS indent/outdent/move commands, with Shift+F10 support.

records.claim_text: Items can be repositioned within a table or moved to other UI elements by drag and drop, with drop targets on items, between items, or both.
records.evidence_quote: Drop targets can be on items, between items, or both
records.own_words_restatement: Dropping on a node reparents; dropping between nodes reorders. Both must be distinguishable.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Defines WBS move semantics: on-node = reparent, between-nodes = resequence.

records.claim_text: Percentage or auto column widths cause other columns to resize and can shift positions, whereas pixel-based widths affect only the resized column.
records.evidence_quote: resizing one column might also lead to the automatic resizing of some
records.own_words_restatement: Choose fixed units for predictable resize behaviour, relative units to avoid trailing whitespace.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Persisted WBS column widths should be stored in fixed units.

records.claim_text: SAP prescribes sorting status information by severity: ascending runs positive to negative with neutral last, descending is the exact reverse.
records.evidence_quote: Ascending: Sort status information from positive to negative, with neutral last.
records.own_words_restatement: Status columns sort by meaning rather than alphabetically, with a defined place for neutral.
records.applicability_to_our_build: WBS status column needs an explicit severity ordinal, not string sort.

records.claim_text: Export is triggered from a split menu button on the table toolbar with an Export As dialog reachable via Shift+Ctrl+E.
records.evidence_quote: For Export As…, use the shortcut: Shift+Ctrl+E
records.own_words_restatement: One click exports with remembered settings; the dropdown half opens the settings dialog.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Directly implementable in the WBS toolbar.

records.claim_text: SAP's own learning platform confirms the flexible column layout is intended for list-detail drilldown scenarios rather than tool-style workbenches.
records.evidence_quote: master-detail or master-detail-detail scenario in which the user can drill down or navigate
records.own_words_restatement: Second first-party source agreeing that the column layout is a drilldown device.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Corroborates R09-089.

records.claim_text: The canonical Fiori for Web guidelines are served from www.sap.com/design-system and return HTTP 403 to non-browser HTTP clients while rendering normally in a real browser.
records.evidence_quote: The server returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.
records.own_words_restatement: Edge bot protection blocks plain fetchers; the in-app browser renders the same URLs and exposes a full page index at /edge/design-system/fiori-design-web/query-index.json.
records.applicability_to_our_build: Methodological note for future research lanes: use the browser tool, and drive URLs from the query-index.json page manifest.

search_log.query_or_url: WebSearch: SAP accessibility conformance WCAG 2.2 Level AA EN 301 549 product standard SAP Fiori
search_log.result: WEAK - only third-party accessibility vendors returned; no first-party SAP page stating a conformance level was found. Recorded as a gap

gaps: ACCESSIBILITY CONFORMANCE LEVEL: SAP's Fiori accessibility product-standard page names WCAG 2.2 as the reference standard and cites the 7:1 high-contrast text ratio, but does NOT state a conformance level (A/AA/AAA) or reference EN 301 549 on that page. Searched: the design-system accessibility product-standard page, the screen-reader page, the keyboard-support page, and a general web search on 2026-08-05. No first-party level statement located. Do not assert 'SAP Fiori is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant' downstream without a VPAT citation.

RIGHT-TO-LEFT: the SAP Fiori for Web design guidelines contain no dedicated RTL article (verified by filtering the full 8142-entry site page index). RTL guidance exists only in SAPUI5 developer documentation, which is implementation-level, not design-level. There is therefore no first-party Fiori *design* rule about mirroring tree indentation or expand/collapse chevrons; R09-076 is an inference from the general directionality statement.

KEYBOARD KEY TABLES: the v1-148 keyboard-support foundation page states principles and then defers all concrete key mappings to Figma design-specification frames, which are not fetchable. Concrete table keybindings were recovered only incidentally from the tree-table and grid-table articles (Shift+arrow resize, Ctrl+arrow reorder, Ctrl+A select all, Shift+F10 context menu, Ctrl+Enter create, Shift+Ctrl+E export). A complete Fiori keyboard map could not be evidenced.

SAP FIORI ELEMENTS FEATURE MATRICES: three pages (table-types, table-features, tables-toolbar under discover/frameworks/sap-fiori-elements) store their content as escaped HTML comparison tables. They render for a human but do not yield clean quotable sentences, so per-feature availability claims (which table types support freeze, grouping, Export to PDF, Clear All defaults) are readable but NOT cited here. If a downstream section needs the exact FE feature matrix, it must be re-read visually.

P13N DIALOG: /v1-148/ui-elements/p13n-dialog/usage exists in the site index but returned no extractable text on 2026-08-05. Its content is covered indirectly by the table-personalization overview page.

NO NUMERIC ROW-COUNT GUIDANCE FOR TREE DEPTH: SAP gives a 1000-item scroll optimisation boundary and a 200-item responsive-table ceiling, but states no maximum hierarchy DEPTH for a tree table. The only depth-related figures found were 'no more than four levels deep' as a phone fallback heuristic and 'first seven levels' for spreadsheet export grouping.

THEME VALUES DELIBERATELY NOT CAPTURED: per the SAP IP rule, no theme hex values, colour parameter values, screenshots or asset URLs were recorded. Theming records describe the token/theme architecture as a concept only.
